prompt: Real-estate listings change hourly and must be indexed by search engines with their current prices.
why: Render on the server per request so crawlers get fresh, complete HTML.
trap: Static generation would serve stale prices between builds.

prompt: A logged-in dashboard shows each user's own data, and a blank screen while JavaScript loads feels slow.
why: SSR sends meaningful HTML for that user on first response.
trap: Personalized per user rules out pre-building pages.

prompt: Shared links to a single-page app show no title or image in chat previews, because the HTML is empty until JavaScript runs.
tells: no title or image in chat previews
HTML is empty until JavaScript runs
why: Link-preview bots don't run JS; server-render the page or at least its meta tags.
trap: Images aren't the problem; the HTML is empty.

prompt: A page's HTML takes 900 ms to arrive because the server waits on three APIs before sending anything. Users see nothing until then.
tells: waits on three APIs before sending anything
why: Stream the server-rendered HTML: send the shell first, then fill in sections as data arrives.
trap: SSR is the right call; blocking on all data isn't.

prompt: A store shows prices in the visitor's currency based on their location, and search engines must see real prices on first load.
tells: search engines must see real prices
why: Each request needs different HTML, rendered on the server.
trap: Pre-built pages can't vary by visitor.

prompt: A dashboard flashes the logged-out view for half a second before JavaScript checks the session and redirects.
why: Check the session on the server and render (or redirect) before sending HTML.
trap: The flash comes from deciding in the browser.

prompt: Shareable search result URLs like /search?q=boots should show results immediately and be indexable.
why: The query isn't known at build time; render per request.
trap: You can't pre-build every possible query.

prompt: A server-rendered page logs hydration warnings because the server printed one timestamp and the browser rendered another.
why: SSR output must match the first client render; render times on one side only, or pass the value through.
trap: It's an SSR pitfall, not a reason to drop SSR.
